metadata.purpose: The corpus's editorial methodology — claim types, six-source minimum, editorial passes.

data.title: Editorial methodology
data.prose: Wheel of Heaven is a working hypothesis offered to be tested. The methodology supporting that posture is concrete and machine-readable. Every page declares its claim type (direct, inferred, or speculative). Every new entry meets a six-source minimum spanning Raëlian, primary, scholarly, scientific, comparative, and critical layers. Every major rewrite under a given editorial pass is tagged with the pass's date code so future readers can tell at a glance which entries reflect the current framing.

claim_types.use_for: The claim is explicit in a primary source, or is a direct description of the project / methodology, or is scientifically established.
Reasonable reading of a source, not literally stated but consistent with it. Comparative-religion readings; framework summaries.
Interpretive synthesis or hypothesis that goes beyond what any single source states. Honesty about reach — not a weakness.

target_breakdown: 1 source from a comparative tradition (Tier 1, different family)
six_source_rule.scope: Hard gate on new entries. Existing entries from before the rule are grandfathered (flagged legacy_pre_six_source).
six_source_rule.exemptions: Newsroom dispatches are exempt — they require only the primary news source(s) plus at least one canon link.

editorial_passes.description: Date-coded marker (YYYY-MM) recording the editorial campaign under which an entry was last fundamentally rewritten. Lets readers tell whether an entry reflects current framing or pre-dates a major reframe.
editorial_passes.current_pass_summary: First major pass under the modern, working-hypothesis, human-civilization framing. Drops 'democratization' / 'knowledge base' / 'lore' register; tightens claim discipline; uses 'Elohim were a small advanced human civilization' rather than 'extraterrestrial'.

translations.translation_program: The WoH Translation Program produces -woh translations of foundational texts (genesis-woh, exodus-woh, etc.) with machine-readable provenance: source text edition, glossary version, model versions used in drafting, reviewer, and lexical divergences from base translations. See /v1/translations/.
